title: GH#33054: fix(oauth-pool): show OAuth URL and read auth code from terminal in console sessions
body:
Resolves #33054

## Summary

In console-only sessions, `model-accounts-pool add` did not print the OAuth URL, and the pasted authorization code was lost. This PR fixes it at the root:

- `open_browser()` (`.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh`) always prints the URL first. It skips launchers when there is no graphical display (Linux without `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/WSL), so `xdg-open` cannot fall back to lynx/w3m. Launchers now run with detached stdio (`</dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1`), so they can no longer consume the terminal's stdin or write into the `$(...)` capture pipe.
- New `oauth_prompt_read()` prompts and reads on `/dev/tty` when a controlling terminal exists and falls back to stderr/stdin for headless use. It is used by `_add_prompt_email`, `_add_read_auth_code` and `cmd_add_google` (`.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh`).

## Reproducer

With a fake `xdg-open` in PATH that prints to stdout and runs `cat >/dev/null`, pipe `THECODE#NONCE` into `_cmd_add_pkce_authorize`:

- before: `[ERROR] No authorization code provided`, exit 1 (with or without `DISPLAY`);
- after: the URL is printed, the prompt is shown and the result is `rc=0 code=[THECODE]` in both GUI and console modes. Under a pty (`script -qec`) the prompt waits on `/dev/tty` as expected.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh`: clean
- `bash tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh`: 13 passed, 0 failed
- Pre-commit quality validation: passed

## Regression Evidence

This fix needs an interactive controlling terminal (`/dev/tty`) and a real browser launcher (`xdg-open`/`open`/`wslview`). CI runners have no controlling terminal and no display, so a repository test cannot exercise the interactive prompt path in any meaningful way. The regression was reproduced and verified manually instead, using the fake-launcher harness described under Reproducer (non-tty fallback path) and `script -qec` (pty path, where the prompt is shown on `/dev/tty`). The old code fails in both GUI and console modes; the new code passes. The existing `tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh` suite still passes (13/13).

## Notes

- The earlier `--no-open` PR #18846 was closed as completed via #18977, but that PR never carried the URL change. Automatic display detection plus always printing the URL covers the same use case without a flag.

title: perf(gh-shim): attribute and reduce REST read overhead (#33062)

Resolves #33062

## Summary

Attributes and reduces `gh` shim REST read overhead without changing quota admission, trust boundaries, or write checks.

- Opt-in, value-free phase timing: `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_TIMING=1` (phase names and durations only; never arguments, tokens, headers, or bodies).
- Removed the per-call Python `realpath` spawn in `_shim_canonical_path` (pure-bash resolution was already the fallback).
- REST metadata parsing: three `jq` invocations → one, reused for the final attempt log.
- Plain `gh api ENDPOINT [--jq|-q EXPR]` GET fast path: skips loading write-policy, label-provisioning, and guard libraries. Any other shape (fields, `--input`, `-X/--method`, `--paginate`, `graphql`, `graphql/*`) keeps the full policy path.

## Acceptance revision (interactive maintainer decision)

The original ≤150 ms added-overhead target is not reachable without structural change. It is replaced with: **measured mechanical reduction on the plain-read path, plus profiling that attributes the remaining cost**. Reasoning:

Governed REST read (`repos/.../issues/N --jq .state`), phase timing on, three runs:

| Phase | ms |
| --- | --- |
| Bash startup, library loads, preflight (≈10 ms Perl clock per marker included) | ~185 (≈85 real) |
| Governor Python startup/imports | ~58 |
| `credential_identity` (`gh auth token` spawn) | ~60 |
| SQLite open + admission | ~6 |
| **Deliberate quota pacing** | **287–1170** |
| Native `gh` child | 388–601 |
| Metadata parse + telemetry append | ~65 |

Mechanical overhead is ≈270 ms. Wall time is dominated by deliberate pacing, because the shared REST-core pool runs at ~3,500–4,150 of 5,000/h. Credential lookup stays per call on purpose: the token is pinned only to the native child, never exported to long-lived parents. The larger throughput levers are fewer calls: #33068 (caller attribution) and #32638 (dispatch ceremony).

Wall time, timing off, zero-cost `rate_limit` read, 9 runs per variant, 2 rounds (medians, ms):

| Variant | Round 1 | Round 2 | Added vs native |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native `gh` | 323 | 313 | — |
| Deployed shim (main) | 678 | 729 | 355–416 |
| This branch | 617 | 662 | 294–349 |

This is ≈60 ms (~15%) less mechanical overhead per plain read. For governed reads the saving is smaller than pacing variance, as expected.

## Worker evidence (retained)

The worker's earlier serial and concurrent measurements showed native 368–497 ms vs shim 764–7001 ms. The concurrent spread matched deliberate pacing (396–5921 ms), while SQLite admission itself took 4–64 ms.

title: GH#33068: perf(gh-api): attribute timeout-wrapped and session-origin REST calls
body:
Resolves #33068

## Root cause (sampled evidence)

I sampled live `gh` shim processes for 4 minutes on the maintainer runner and replayed the shim's own caller algorithm on each (script: process basenames only, no arguments):

- 169 distinct REST shim processes: 94 attributed from a parent script, **75 (44%) generic**.
- **All 75** had `timeout` as their immediate parent: `timeout < pulse-merge-routine.sh` 51, `timeout < pulse-wrapper.sh` 24.

`_shim_parent_framework_caller` only looked through shell/env launchers. `timeout 30 gh api …` is the framework's standard read pattern, so every timeout-wrapped call fell back to `gh_api_rest`. That also explains the `pulse-review-explicit-page` rows the issue flagged.

## Change (`.agents/scripts/gh-native-transport-lib.sh` only)

1. Walk past transparent process wrappers (`timeout`, `gtimeout`, `nice`, `nohup`, `stdbuf`, `caffeinate`), at most 3 levels, with one `ps -o ppid=,command=` per level. The command-line matching moved unchanged into `_shim_command_framework_caller`.
2. Session-role fallback: when no framework script is found, map the already-exported `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ORIGIN` through a fixed allowlist (`worker`, `interactive`, `pulse`, `routine`, `conversation`) to `session-<role>`. Values are never copied verbatim; anything else keeps the subcommand label.
3. Precedence: `AIDEVOPS_GH_CALLER` (framework file) → parent framework script → session role → subcommand label.

No new session-start exports were needed: workers (`pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`, `headless-runtime-run.sh`), the OpenCode plugin (interactive), and the launcher (conversation) already export `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ORIGIN`. The caller value is logging-only; quota admission, pacing, and trust behaviour are unchanged. Step 4 of the brief (per-process parent-lookup cache) is not applicable, because each shim process resolves its caller once.

## Verification

Throwaway harness: a real process tree `framework-script → [wrapper] → shim-stand-in`, with `_SHIM_DIR` containing the framework script:

| Case | Old (deployed) | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| direct | `fake-framework-caller.sh` | `fake-framework-caller.sh` |
| `timeout` | `gh_api_rest` | `fake-framework-caller.sh` |
| `nice timeout` | `gh_api_rest` | `fake-framework-caller.sh` |
| `$(timeout …)` | `gh_api_rest` | `fake-framework-caller.sh` |
| no framework parent, origin unset | — | `gh_api_rest` |
| no framework parent, origin=worker | — | `session-worker` |
| origin=`worker;rm` (injection) | — | `gh_api_rest` |
| framework parent + origin=worker | — | framework script wins |

title: t18558: fix(prefetch): bound events-tickle skip by snapshot age (GH#33074)
body:
Resolves #33074

## Summary

The batch prefetch skipped an owner's refresh whenever the L1 events tickle returned 304. For organisations the tickle polls `/orgs/{org}/events`, which lists **public events only**. On a maintainer install with a private-repo org among its pulse owners, the ETag had not changed since 2026-08-19. The tickle reported "fresh" 48 times in a row, and that org's canonical issue and PR snapshots were 18–22 days stale.

Effects measured before this change:

- **API volume:** consumers fell back to a live `_prefetch_single_repo: full sweep` (non-conditional list reads) for that repo every cycle, instead of zero-cost conditional 304s.
- **Dispatch time (#32638):** the #33044 worker-draft negative cache needs a PR snapshot less than 900 s old, so it could never cache that repo's draft checkpoints. In 12 h, five of its issues were re-rejected 17–19 times each (6.6–10.9 min of dedup ceremony per issue). Repeat-rejected candidates (at least 5 attempts, never launched) accounted for 75% of all `dedup_check` time (160.9 min). Draft checkpoints on user-owned repos in the same window *were* cached.

## Change

- `pulse-events-tickle.sh`: `_PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_LAST_REASON` records why the call returned 0: `etag` (304) or `cooldown` (preflight, rate-limited response, or rate-limited org retry). The header documents the public-events limitation.
- `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh`:
  - `_resolve_cache_snapshot` takes an optional max-age argument (default unchanged).
  - New `_owner_snapshots_recent` and `_events_tickle_skip_is_safe`.
  - `_cmd_refresh` honours cooldown skips as before. It honours ETag skips only while every owner snapshot is younger than `PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_MAX_CACHE_AGE` (default 900 s, the dispatch fingerprint bound). Otherwise it logs `events tickle fresh for owner=… but snapshots older than 900s — refreshing`, counts the owner as stale, and runs the normal conditional-REST refresh.
- `TODO.md`: t18558 entry.

A refresh that ignores the tickle costs at most two conditional GETs per repo. Those are free 304s when nothing changed.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-batch-prefetch-conditional-rest.sh`: 31/31 pass, including three new cases:
  - an ETag 304 with stale snapshots refreshes (2 repo calls, snapshot restamped);
  - an ETag 304 with recent snapshots still skips (0 repo calls);
  - a cooldown still skips even with stale snapshots.
- **Negative control:** the same test run against `origin/main` versions of the two scripts fails the stale case with `repo_calls=0, prs_ts=2026-05-01T00:00:00Z`, which is the production symptom. The other two cases pass on both.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-events-tickle.sh`: 32/32.
- `test-pulse-prefetch-canonical-snapshot.sh`, `test-pulse-cache-prime.sh`, `test-pulse-batch-refresh-timeout.sh`, `test-pulse-rate-limit-config-precedence.sh`: pass. `test-gh-api-instrument.sh`: 244/244; one earlier run hit a timing flake in an unrelated function-timeout case.
- `test-enrich-batch-prefetch.sh` fails the same two REST-fallback cases on unmodified `origin/main`, so it is pre-existing and not a regression.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-events-tickle.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh`: clean.

## Post-deploy check

`pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh status` should show the private-org snapshots FRESH, and `pulse.log` should show `cross-cycle ownership block:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` for that repo's draft-checkpoint issues.

title: t18561: fix(migrate-layout): skip verification for zero-row OpenCode DB consumers
body:
## Summary

`aidevops repos migrate-layout apply` failed with `OpenCode database verification failed: <isolated opencode.db>` after it had already moved the repository and updated the main OpenCode DB. The receipt was left partial.

## Root cause

The plan lists every isolated `opencode-interactive/*/opencode/opencode.db` as a database consumer. It keeps DBs with zero matching rows too, because they act as drift guards. Those DBs have an empty change set. `database_change_state()` reports an empty set as `"before"`, so `update_database()` ran an empty transaction. Its post-check then required `"after"` and raised. Any install with an unrelated isolated OpenCode DB hits this.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py` `update_database()`: return early when `details["changes"]` is empty. `rollback_database()` already treats an empty set as `"before"` and returns, so rollback is unchanged.
- `tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py`: the fixture now adds a second isolated DB that points at an unrelated path, giving a consumer with zero rows. The consumer-boundary resume test now also covers `consumer:database:2`.

## Verification

- Before the fix, the updated fixture reproduced the exact field error: 12 of 13 tests failed with `OpenCode database verification failed: .../isolated/worker-2/opencode/opencode.db`.
- After the fix, `python3 -W ignore::ResourceWarning tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py` passed all 13 tests.

title: GH#32977: fix: reserve declared file footprints atomically within each Pulse refill batch
body:
## Summary

Implementation for issue #32977: a Pulse refill batch no longer launches two workers whose declared file footprints overlap.

Before this change, each candidate ran its own dispatch subshell with a cold footprint cache. A worker only became visible to the overlap check once its status labels landed on GitHub, so overlapping candidates in one refill batch could both pass `_footprint_check_overlap`.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
  - Adds a per-repo reservation store (`~/.aidevops/cache/footprint-reservations`, 0700). Filenames use a hashed repo key, so private repo names never appear on disk. A per-repo `mkdir` lock breaks stale holders.
  - `_footprint_check_overlap` reads live labels outside the lock, then under the lock merges active reservations and checks overlap. If there is no overlap, it atomically writes this candidate's reservation (temp file, then `mv`). If the lock stays busy, it defers the candidate to the next cycle.
  - `status:queued` now counts as in-flight, both for live footprints and for the durable-defer blocker lifecycle.
  - Reservations end in one of three ways:
    - Released on a failed launch (`footprint_release_reservation`, scoped to the current attempt's epoch).
    - Stamped `superseded_at` once the issue's lifecycle labels are visible, then removed after a 120s grace period. The grace keeps a concurrent caller with a stale live read from missing it.
    - Expired after a 900s TTL.
  - Shared release/version files (`VERSION`, `CHANGELOG.md`, …) are low-information and do not block on their own. Any shared implementation file still blocks.
  - Bare list items in a canonical `## Files Scope` / `### Files Scope` section now count as a declared footprint. Paths elsewhere stay context-only.
  - Moves the parallel active-label fetch into `_footprint_fetch_active_issues`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: `_dispatch_process_candidate` releases this attempt's reservation when dispatch fails or times out, and when launch validation fails.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`: batch-reservation cases required by the issue acceptance criteria.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (dispatch gating)
- **Live read-only check** against `marcusquinn/aidevops` with temp reservation/defer stores and no GitHub writes:

title: GH#33132: fix: surface one approval-ready attention record when a blocked worker leaves a draft checkpoint
body:
## Summary

Resolves #33132

A worker that releases as `blocked` after opening a draft PR leaves the objective held by `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT`. That hold is intentional: a blocked checkpoint must never auto-continue without the revision-bound approval from GH#31265 / PR #31269. But until now nothing told the brief owner that an approval (or a draft close) was the required next step, so the objective stalled silently.

This PR keeps the approval-bound invariant and adds no continuation path. When Pulse hits the draft checkpoint block, it now asks the continuation helper to post **one** deduplicated, actionable attention record.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: new `blocked-attention <repo> <issue> <pr>` command.
  - Posts only when the draft is open, the newest trusted `CLAIM_RELEASED` is the PR author's `reason=blocked` release, and no later coordination event (claim, lease, dispatch, release, interactive claim) shows another owner.
  - Deduplicates by PR head and release ID via a hidden marker.
  - Names the release comment ID and the original ready-lease attempt, so the `approval-template` command in the body is ready to run. It lists both exits: correct the brief and approve, or close the draft to restart ordinary dispatch.
  - No body line starts with a coordination or approval prefix, so `pr_checkpoint_events` release/successor validation for a later approval is unaffected. It grants nothing, changes no labels or assignees, and never dispatches.
  - The usage text now lists every subcommand.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`: layer 4 calls the helper on a best-effort basis before returning the existing `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` block (rc 2 is unchanged).
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`: documents the attention record.
